notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words, and from nothing else: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims. Where the Quran leaves a person unnamed or names only a title, the draft keeps them unnamed; identifications and later-tradition names appear only in the unknowns and uncertainties. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: When Isa sensed disbelief from them, he asked who would be his helpers toward God.
The disciples said that they were God's helpers, that they believed in God, and asked him to bear witness that they submit.
They said, our Lord, we believe in what You sent down and have followed the messenger, so write us down among the witnesses.

chapters.summary_md: When Isa sensed disbelief from them, he asked who would be his helpers toward God [c1]. The disciples said that they were God's helpers and that they believed in God [c2]. They prayed to be written down among the witnesses [c3].
chapters.body_md: When Isa sensed disbelief from them, he asked who would be his helpers toward God [c1]. The disciples said that they were God's helpers, that they believed in God, and asked him to bear witness that they submit [c2]. They said, our Lord, we believe in what You sent down and have followed the messenger, so write us down among the witnesses [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah gives the disciples' answer in parts, an address to Isa and a prayer to their Lord [c2][c3]. The word for submit, muslimun, is rendered by its general sense here [c2].
chapters.kids_md: Isa asked who would be his helpers toward God [c1]. The disciples said that they were God's helpers [c2]. They prayed to be written down among the witnesses [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the disciples answer a call for help with a statement of belief and a prayer [c2][c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who they were, how many, or where this took place.
- Not established: from whom Isa sensed disbelief, beyond the word them.
- Not established: what the word hawariyyun means in its origin; the ayat use it without explaining it.

claims.statement_en: God says that He inspired the disciples to believe in Him and in His messenger, and that they said that they believed and asked Him to bear witness that they submit.

chapters.summary_md: God says that He inspired the disciples to believe in Him and in His messenger [c1]. They said that they believed and asked Him to bear witness that they submit [c1].
chapters.body_md: God says that He inspired the disciples to believe in Him and in His messenger, and that they said that they believed and asked Him to bear witness that they submit [c1].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah speaks of an inspiration to the disciples, and the verb is the one used for inspiration generally [c1]. It does not say how the inspiration came [c1].
chapters.kids_md: God inspired the disciples to believe in Him and in His messenger [c1]. They said that they believed [c1].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayah presents the disciples' belief as something God inspired [c1].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: how the inspiration came to them.
- Not established in this ayah: who the messenger is; the ayah does not name him.

claims.statement_en: God tells the believers to be helpers of God, as Isa, son of Maryam, said to the disciples, who are my helpers toward God, and the disciples said that they were God's helpers.
One group of the Children of Israel believed and another group disbelieved, and God supported those who believed against their enemy, and they became prevailing.

chapters.summary_md: God tells the believers to be helpers of God, as Isa, son of Maryam, said to the disciples [c1]. One group of the Children of Israel believed and another disbelieved [c2]. God supported those who believed against their enemy [c2].
chapters.body_md: God tells the believers to be helpers of God, as Isa, son of Maryam, said to the disciples, who are my helpers toward God, and the disciples said that they were God's helpers [c1]. One group of the Children of Israel believed and another group disbelieved, and God supported those who believed against their enemy, and they became prevailing [c2].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah recalls the call of Isa as an example for the believers [c1]. The Arabic word rendered prevailing can also mean uppermost or manifest, and the ayah does not say in what way they prevailed [c2].
chapters.kids_md: Isa, son of Maryam, asked the disciples who would be his helpers toward God [c1]. The disciples said that they were God's helpers [c1]. One group of the Children of Israel believed and another group did not [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayah asks the believers to answer as the disciples answered [c1]. Another is that it ends by recording that God supported those who believed [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the enemy was, or when this support came.
- Not established: in what way those who believed prevailed.
- Not established: the numbers in the groups, or how they divided.

uncertainties_en: Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the disciples are numbered and named in later works, with their occupations and their travels.
Hadith to add later: reports about the disciples of Isa, with a named grader for each; none is used here.
